ptsd_229 eng I’ll describe this as carefully as I can, because for a long time I couldn’t describe it at all.

I was 34, a primary school teacher, married, no children yet. My husband and I had been trying for a baby for two years without success and it was putting a lot of strain on us. A close friend of mine had done a psilocybin retreat in the Netherlands and came back glowing, saying it had helped her let go of years of grief. I booked the same retreat, partly hoping it would help me with the stress of trying to conceive, and partly, I think, because I wanted to feel something other than disappointment for a weekend.

The retreat was in a renovated farmhouse. There were ten participants and three facilitators, all very warm. On the first evening we sat in a circle and shared our intentions. I said I wanted to make peace with not being in control of my body. Everyone nodded. The facilitators talked about ‘surrender’ and ‘trusting the medicine’.

The ceremony began the next morning. We drank truffle tea, lay down on mats with eyeshades, and the music began. The dose was high. I remember the come-up as a kind of heavy, sweet sinking, as if the floor were turning into honey. For about an hour it was beautiful. I saw fields of flowers, I felt my body as warm and alive, I cried softly about the babies I hadn’t had.

Then the flowers turned into something else. They became wombs, hundreds of them, opening and closing, and every one was empty. I heard a sound like a heartbeat, but it was slowing, slowing, until it stopped. I understood, with absolute certainty, that I would never have a child. That my body was a barren place, that I had been born broken. The certainty was total. It wasn’t a thought, it was a knowledge that went through every cell.

Then something worse happened. I started to see children, not my children, but children I knew: the children in my class. I saw their faces, one after another, and each one turned grey and still. I felt that I was being shown that I was a danger to children, that something in me was poisonous, that this was why my body wouldn’t let me have one. I know how irrational this sounds now, but in that state it was the most real truth I’d ever encountered.

I tore off my eyeshade. The room was full of people lying on mats, and the facilitators moving quietly between them, and it looked like a field hospital, or a morgue. A facilitator came over and asked what was happening. I couldn’t explain. I said ‘I’m poison, I’m poison’ over and over. She put her hand on my belly, I think meaning to comfort me, and I screamed, because that was exactly the place where the poison was.

I tried to get up and leave, but my legs wouldn’t hold me, and I fell against the wall. Two facilitators guided me to a smaller side room with a mattress and stayed with me. One of them held my hand. I was sobbing so hard that I couldn’t breathe properly, and I started to hyperventilate, and my hands cramped into claws. I thought I was dying. Part of me wanted to.

I went somewhere after that. I don’t know how long it lasted. There was no room, no facilitators, no me. Just an endless grey plain with a cold wind, and the knowledge that I was alone and would always be alone, and that nothing would ever grow there. I wandered on that plain for what felt like years.

When I came back, it was afternoon. The facilitators were still there. One of them was crying too. They had been with me for five hours. They gave me water and a blanket and sat with me until the evening. In the closing circle I couldn’t speak. My friend’s glowing description of the retreat kept going through my head like a cruel joke.

I went home the next day. I told my husband it had been ‘intense’. I didn’t tell him the rest for months. 		3 3 3 3 3 3 2 0

ptsd_003 eng Persistent depersonalisation and derealisation for almost two years. I would look in the mirror and not recognise myself, or I’d see myself but feel nothing, like looking at a stranger. Fourth, intrusive memories of the hospital, especially the moment I was strapped to a bed in the ER. I’d have flashbacks to that out of nowhere, and I’d get very upset when I saw ambulances or heard sirens. I had nightmares about being trapped in the bathtub, with the water running and running.

They came especially when I was in bright light, on snowy days, or in white rooms like hospitals. During these episodes I’d lose my sense of who I was for a few seconds, and that terrified me.

I had nightmares about the cabin, the tall figures in the corners, the matches turning into insects. I couldn’t stand being in small wooden rooms or being alone in the countryside.

I became very depressed. I was ashamed of my arrogance and the risk I had taken. I’d always seen myself as a responsible, experienced psychonaut, and that identity was shattered. My friend who called the rescue was angry with me for a long time. I felt that I’d betrayed everyone who cared about me.

ptsd_229 eng The aftermath was in some ways worse than the ceremony itself, because it went on for so long and because I couldn’t tell anyone.

The certainty that I would never have a child stayed. Rationally I knew that the trip couldn’t predict anything about my fertility, but the feeling was so deep that I couldn’t shake it. Every month, when my period came, it felt like confirmation. I stopped believing the doctors when they said there was still a good chance. I became withdrawn and listless, and I started to dread the fertility appointments that I used to approach with hope.

Worse was the belief that I was poisonous to children. I’m a teacher, and for months I struggled to be in the classroom. I’d look at the children and see their faces turning grey, the way they did in the trip. I’d feel a wave of nausea and have to leave the room. I avoided hugging them or touching their shoulders, which I’d always done naturally. I felt like a danger to them. I know now this was intrusive thinking, but at the time I thought it might be true. I didn’t tell anyone because I was terrified someone would think I was actually dangerous.

I had panic attacks, especially at night and before work. I had nightmares about empty wombs and grey plains. I had a constant tightness in my belly.

My relationship with my husband suffered badly. I couldn’t explain why I was so distant. He thought I was angry with him about the infertility. We stopped having sex, which of course also stopped our attempts to conceive. He suggested couples therapy, and I refused because I was afraid of what I’d have to say.

After about four months I took sick leave from school. I told my doctor I was burnt out. That was partly true. I spent most days on the sofa, staring at the wall. I had thoughts that my husband would be better off with someone else, someone who could give him children and wasn’t poison.

ptsd_003 eng I’ve tried a lot of things. First I contacted the retreat center, who told me I needed to come back and drink again to integrate the experience. I didn’t. That felt very harmful and I’ve since learned other people had similar experiences there.

I found an integration therapist through a psychedelic harm reduction organisation. That was the first thing that helped a bit, mostly because she didn’t think I was crazy and she knew others who had been through similar things. We did weekly sessions for about a year.

I also saw a psychiatrist who put me on an SSRI (escitalopram), which helped the depression a little, and quetiapine for sleep, which helped me sleep but made me feel even more like a zombie. I stopped the quetiapine after a few months.

Meditation made things much worse at first. Every time I closed my eyes and focused inward I felt like I was slipping back into the void. A teacher at a meditation center told me to ‘sit with it’ and I had a panic attack in the middle of the session. Later, with my therapist, I tried very gentle body-based practices with eyes open, which were OK.

Exercise helped, especially running, because it made me feel my body. Being in nature during the day also helped.

Honestly the biggest factor has been time. It’s been almost three years and I’m much better, but I’m not the same as before and I’m still struggling with the existential side of it. 		3 2 2 2 2 0 2 2 0

ptsd_027 eng After the incident I finally got into the VA system properly. My lawyer helped push that. I was assigned a psychiatrist and a therapist. The first therapist did prolonged exposure therapy, which was brutal, especially at the beginning, but it did help with the nightmares. I was put on prazosin for nightmares, which helped a lot, and sertraline, which I’m not sure did much. I tried several other medications for sleep that made me groggy and I stopped them.

I went to an inpatient program for veterans with PTSD and substance use for eight weeks. That was the turning point. Being around other guys who understood, getting sober, having structure. I’ve been sober for 14 months now.

My wife and I did couples counselling, which helped her understand what was going on and helped me move back into our bedroom. I’ve been slowly rebuilding my relationship with my kids. My daughter and I do Saturday mornings at the park now, just the two of us.

I joined a peer support group for veterans that meets weekly. That has been very important. I also go fishing with a couple of buddies from the group.

Harmful: the underground session itself, obviously. Also, early on, a VA doctor who basically told me I’d brought it on myself by taking illegal drugs. That made me want to give up on the whole system.

ptsd_205 eng After the hospital I was referred to a community mental health team. I had a care coordinator who visited every two weeks, and a psychiatrist who prescribed an antidepressant and, for the first two months, a low-dose antipsychotic, which I think helped with the presence. After that I had a course of CBT with a psychologist. She was very good. She helped me understand that the presence was a kind of threat-detection gone into overdrive, and we did exercises like sitting with my back to the door on purpose.

Living with my parents was hard but also stabilising. My mum and I eventually talked properly, and she told me how scared she’d been. That helped us both.

I started volunteering at an animal shelter, which got me out of the house and gave me structure. Eventually I got a new job.

Unhelpful: reading forums where people described never recovering from bad trips. Also, a friend who suggested a ‘healing’ mushroom trip to undo the bad one.

I’m a lot better now, two years later. I still don’t like mirrors in the evening. 		3 1 2 2 0 0 2 1 0

ptsd_229 eng Once I’d told my husband, things started to move. My GP referred me to a psychologist, who recognised quickly that I was having intrusive thoughts and that they are very common and don’t mean anything about who I am. That was a huge relief. We did CBT for the intrusive thoughts, with exposure, which was terrifying at first, for example spending time in the classroom and allowing the thoughts to come without leaving. Over months it became easier.

My husband and I did couples therapy, which helped us reconnect and talk about the infertility honestly. I also started an antidepressant, after discussing it with the fertility clinic.

I wrote to the retreat about what happened. They were kind and apologetic, which I didn’t expect, and offered a free integration session, which I declined.

I went back to teaching after five months. I’m doing much better. We’re still trying for a baby, and I still have hard days, but I no longer believe what the trip told me. 		3 1 0 2 0 0 2 1 0

dataset original translation
APEQ Die Depression ist weg. Einfach weg. Ich kann es selbst kaum glauben. The depression is gone. Simply gone. I can hardly believe it myself.
APEQ Ich wurde mir bewusst, wie ich in Gesprächen oft nur darauf warte, selbst zu reden, statt zuzuhören. Auch in meiner Familie habe ich Muster erkannt, die sich über Generationen wiederholen, z.B. dass bei uns nie über Gefühle gesprochen wird. Das beschäftigt mich seitdem sehr. I became aware of how, in conversations, I often just wait for my turn to talk instead of listening. I also recognised patterns in my family that repeat over generations, e.g. that we never talk about feelings. This has been on my mind a lot ever since.
APEQ Ich habe zum ersten Mal bewusst wahrgenommen, wie viel ich über andere urteile, und dass diese Urteile meistens mehr über mich aussagen als über die anderen. For the first time I consciously noticed how much I judge others, and that these judgements usually say more about me than about the others.
APEQ Ich fühle mich wie neu geboren. Die Depression, die mich jahrelang begleitet hat, ist fast verschwunden. Ich kann wieder lachen, mich verlieben, Pläne machen. Ich bin so dankbar. I feel reborn. The depression that was with me for years has almost disappeared. I can laugh again, fall in love, make plans. I am so grateful.
APEQ Ich bin seit der Erfahrung kritischer gegenüber meinem Umfeld und merke, wer es gut mit mir meint und wer nicht. Since the experience I have been more critical of the people around me, and I notice who means well with me and who does not.
APEQ Ich habe die Liebe meiner Eltern gespürt, die ich als Kind nie gespürt habe. I felt my parents’ love, which I never felt as a child.
APEQ Ich habe gemerkt, wie sehr ich mich in Gruppen anpasse und meine Meinung zurückhalte. Das fällt mir jetzt ständig auf. I noticed how much I conform in groups and hold back my opinion. Now I notice it all the time.
APEQ Ich habe einen tiefen Einblick in meine Ängste bekommen und verstanden, dass sie meist aus meiner Vergangenheit kommen, vor allem aus der Zeit, als meine Eltern sich getrennt haben. Seitdem denke ich viel darüber nach und erkenne die Ängste schneller, wenn sie auftauchen. I gained a deep insight into my fears and understood that they mostly come from my past, above all from the time when my parents separated. Since then I have thought about it a lot, and I recognise the fears more quickly when they come up.
APEQ Tiefe Entspannung Deep relaxation
APEQ Ich habe mich und meine Motive viel genauer angeschaut, z.B. warum ich so viel arbeite. Es geht um Anerkennung, nicht um das Geld. I looked much more closely at myself and my motives, e.g. why I work so much. It is about recognition, not about the money.
GCMQ Ich bin fröhlicher und lockerer geworden. I have become more cheerful and relaxed.
GCMQ Etwas ausgeglichener, ansonsten wenig Veränderung. Somewhat more balanced, otherwise little change.
GCMQ Ich bin entspannter und weniger ängstlich. I am more relaxed and less anxious.
GCMQ Etwas stabiler, weniger Grübeln Somewhat more stable, less rumination
GCMQ Auf meine psychische Gesundheit im engeren Sinne hatte die Erfahrung kaum Einfluss. Mir ging es vorher schon ganz gut. The experience had hardly any effect on my mental health in the narrower sense. I was already doing quite well before.
GCMQ Etwas zufriedener Somewhat more content
GCMQ Mir ist vieles egal geworden, was mich früher aufgeregt hat. Ich weiß nicht, ob das gut ist, manchmal fühle ich mich etwas gleichgültig. I have stopped caring about a lot of things that used to upset me. I don’t know if that is good; sometimes I feel somewhat indifferent.
GCMQ Meine psychische Gesundheit hat sich durch die Erfahrung deutlich verbessert, auch wenn das zunächst nicht so aussah. Direkt nach der Erfahrung war ich ziemlich durcheinander, weil so viele Gefühle hochkamen, die ich jahrelang ignoriert hatte. Aber mit der Zeit habe ich gelernt, mit diesen Gefühlen umzugehen, und heute fühle ich mich viel lebendiger und ausgeglichener als vorher. Ich hatte früher oft unerklärliche Erschöpfungszustände und eine Art innere Leere, die ich mir nicht erklären konnte. Die sind weitgehend verschwunden. Ich verstehe mich selbst besser und weiß, was ich brauche, um gesund zu bleiben. Ich bin auch offener geworden für Dinge, die ich früher als esoterisch abgetan hätte, wie Meditation oder Körperarbeit. Das hat mein Leben sehr bereichert. My mental health has improved clearly through the experience, even if it did not look that way at first. Right after the experience I was quite confused, because so many feelings came up that I had ignored for years. But over time I learned to deal with these feelings, and today I feel much more alive and balanced than before. I used to often have unexplained states of exhaustion and a kind of inner emptiness that I could not explain to myself. These have largely disappeared. I understand myself better and know what I need to stay healthy. I have also become more open to things that I would have dismissed as esoteric before, like meditation or bodywork. This has greatly enriched my life.
PTSD Nach der Zeremonie kamen immer mehr Erinnerungen an den Missbrauch hoch, die ich jahrelang verdraengt hatte. Ich hatte Flashbacks im Alltag, z.B. beim Duschen oder wenn mich jemand von hinten beruehrt hat. Ich hatte fast jede Nacht Albtraeume und bin schweissgebadet aufgewacht. Meine Depression wurde viel schlimmer statt besser, ich konnte monatelang nicht arbeiten. Ich hatte auch Suizidgedanken. Gleichzeitig habe ich das Gefuehl, dass diese Erinnerungen irgendwann sowieso gekommen waeren, und dass ich jetzt endlich weiss, was mit mir los ist. Aber der Zeitpunkt und die Art, wie es passiert ist, waren furchtbar. After the ceremony, more and more memories of the abuse came up that I had repressed for years. I had flashbacks in everyday life, e.g. in the shower or when someone touched me from behind. I had nightmares almost every night and woke up drenched in sweat. My depression got much worse instead of better, and I could not work for months. I also had suicidal thoughts. At the same time, I feel that these memories would have come up at some point anyway, and that I now finally know what is going on with me. But the timing and the way it happened were terrible.

This module runs automated data-quality checks (empty columns, SPSS filter variables, category casing, stray whitespace, numbers stored as text, problematic and colliding column names, mixed text encodings, personal information, spreadsheet formatting, and careless responding) on the extracted data files.

We examined 1290 columns across 106 data files.

Issues Identified

113 file/column combinations have at least one issue.

About the personal-information flags. These are pattern matches, not confirmed disclosures, and they are tuned to over-report rather than miss something. Expect false positives:

  • Column names are matched against identifying words in English and other European languages (email, telefoonnummer, geboortedatum, …). A column called phone_number flags whether or not it holds one, and an empty or already-anonymised column flags on its name alone.
  • Values are matched against the shape of an identifier. An IP address pattern also matches a version string or a dotted numeric code; a card-number pattern requires both a real issuer prefix and a checksum, but a long numeric ID can still coincide.
  • Free text is flagged when a column holds long, mostly-distinct prose — the shape open-ended answers take. Most such columns contain no names at all.

A flag means look at this column. Where the data is already de-identified (an ip column reading Anonymized, a name column the authors emptied), no action is needed.

Careless Responding

No file could be screened for careless responding.

What this does not cover. Only 0 of 106 data files could be screened: the rest had no detectable multi-item scale block, or too few respondents. Even in a screened file, these checks only look at multi-item rating scales — the only place where a repeated or flat answer pattern is interpretable. Single questions, open text, demographics and any item outside a detected scale block are never examined. A respondent can therefore answer most of a survey carelessly and still not be flagged here, and finding nothing is not evidence that a dataset is free of careless responding.

Reproducibility Check

We ran the paper’s 7 R scripts in the order they depend on each other, each in an isolated container, for at most 5 minutes per script. Metacheck detected version information that can be used to install specific versions of software for the reproducibility run. We recommend retrying the reproducibility check with recorded_versions = TRUE. This will install the required R packages, if still available. As this takes a long time, this setting is not implemented on this shared server.

3 of 7 scripts ran to the end: 2 stopped with an error, 1 needed a person, 1 needed the internet.

How to make your code run on another computer

We ran your code on a clean computer, the way a reader or reviewer would. Below is each problem we found, the scripts it affects, and how to fix it. Fix them in the order given: a problem near the top can cause the ones below it.

Files are missing from your deposit.

  • extract_spec.R reads e5_APEQ.rds.
  • public_spec.R reads APEQ.rds.

The script stops at the line that reads the file.

  1. Find the file on your computer.
  2. Add it to the deposit, in the folder where the script looks for it.
  3. If you cannot share it, for example for privacy reasons, say so in the README, and explain where readers can get it and where to put it.

A script downloads data while it runs.

  • run_all.R

Online files can move, change or disappear. Save the downloaded files, add them to the deposit, and let the script read the saved copies.

A script waits for a person to choose a file, answer a question, or give arguments on the command line.

  • check_privacy.R

Nobody can answer when the code is checked automatically. Write the file name into the script, and put the exact command with its arguments in the README.

File paths

Every data path in the code works in the repository as deposited. The code reads files that are only inside fguenther/free-text-analysis-psychedelics-v1.zip, and no script unpacks it. We unpacked it in its folder before the run. So that others can run the code as deposited, start the code with a line that unpacks it (such as unzip("free-text-analysis-psychedelics-v1.zip") in R), or upload the files unpacked. 7 data paths were built at runtime with sprintf()/paste()/file.path() instead of written as a literal path — this is fragile authoring practice (it silently breaks if the code is run from a different working directory than the author’s own). We resolved all of these on a best-effort basis.

Files not run on their own

5 files only define functions, so running them on their own says nothing: a function counts when a script uses it. These files are not counted as scripts. 0 are used by no script in the deposit.

Execution

The code was run. Each script ran in an isolated Docker container against a throwaway copy of the repository, in the run order above, with a 300-second per-script timeout. Of 12 scripts: 3 ran without error, 2 errored, 0 timed out, 0 could not run because one of its own dependencies is unavailable, 0 did not parse, and 5 were run by another script with source(). Running against current package versions: a break can reflect version drift, which argues for pinning versions. 1 script needs a person to choose a file, answer a question or use an app, which cannot be reproduced without one: check_privacy.R. Naming the file in the script solves this. 1 script needs the internet, which is off during the run: run_all.R. Keeping what they download in the deposit solves this. 1 script uses an object or function that only another script defines, so in the second run that script was loaded first, in the same session: figures.R after config_data.R. Such a script should source() the other itself, since it does not run on its own.

a script hit an object '...' not found error, indicating it expected a variable another script defines. We inferred which script supplies it and re-ordered so that script runs first, and re-ran once. The outcomes above are from that corrected run.

> ordinal_table <- function(x, d = 0) {
>   tab <- table(x)

>   grp <- as.list(v)
>   while (length(n) > 1 && any(n < MIN_CELL)) {

>     j  <- nb[which.min(n[nb])]
>     lo <- min(i, j); hi <- max(i, j)
>     grp[[lo]] <- c(grp[[lo]], grp[[hi]]); n[lo] <- n[lo] + n[hi]
>     grp[[hi]] <- NULL; n <- n[-hi]

>   N <- length(x)
>   lo_v <- min(v); hi_v <- max(v)

>     if (min(g) == lo_v && max(g) == hi_v) return("all")
>     if (min(g) == lo_v) return(paste0("<=", fmt_num(max(g), d)))
>     if (max(g) == hi_v) return(paste0(">=", fmt_num(min(g), d)))
>     paste0(fmt_num(min(g), d), " to ", fmt_num(max(g), d))
>   }
>   data.frame(
>     value = vapply(grp, label, ""),
>     n = if (length(n) == 1 && n < MIN_CELL) "<10" else as.character(n),

>     stringsAsFactors = FALSE

>     group[pooled] <- "other"

>   keep <- setdiff(lev, pooled)

>     } else {
>       x <- as.numeric(x)
>       if (length(unique(x[!is.na(x)])) < 2) { excluded <- c(excluded, paste(v, "(constant)")); next }
>       cols[[v]] <- x
>     }
>   }
>   list(M = as.data.frame(cols, check.names = FALSE),
>        dummies = do.call(rbind, dummies), excluded = excluded)
> }
> ns_cor <- function(M) {
>   p <- ncol(M); R <- diag(p); dimnames(R) <- list(names(M), names(M))
>   complete <- all(complete.cases(M))
>   if (complete) {
>     S <- vapply(M, normal_scores, numeric(nrow(M)))
>     R <- cor(S); dimnames(R) <- list(names(M), names(M))
>     return(R)
>   }
>   for (i in seq_len(p - 1)) for (j in (i + 1):p) {
>     ok <- !is.na(M[[i]]) & !is.na(M[[j]])
>     R[i, j] <- R[j, i] <- cor(normal_scores(M[[i]][ok]), normal_scores(M[[j]][ok]))
>   }
>   R
> }
> round_pd <- function(R, tol = 1e-4) {
>   min_eig <- function(A) min(eigen(A, symmetric = TRUE, only.values = TRUE)$values)
>   R0 <- round(R, 2)
>   out <- R0; method <- "rounded (already positive definite)"
>   if (min_eig(R0) <= tol) {
>     R1 <- as.matrix(nearPD(R0, corr = TRUE, keepDiag = TRUE, eig.tol = 1e-6, posd.tol = 1e-3)$mat)
>     shrink <- 1
>     repeat {
>       out <- round(R1 * shrink, 2); diag(out) <- 1
>       if (min_eig(out) > tol || shrink < 0.5) break
>       shrink <- shrink - 0.01
>     }
>     method <- sprintf("Matrix::nearPD after rounding, rounded again%s",
>                       if (shrink < 1) sprintf(", off-diagonals shrunk by %.0f%%", 100 * (1 - shrink)) else "")
>   }
>   dimnames(out) <- dimnames(R)
>   list(matrix = out, method = method, min_eigenvalue = round(min_eig(out), 4),
>        max_abs_change = round(max(abs(out - R0)), 2))
> }
> spec_correlation <- function(data, vars, note) {
>   ci <- correlation_inputs(data, vars)
>   R  <- ns_cor(ci$M)
>   pd <- round_pd(R)
>   c(list(variables = colnames(pd$matrix), dummies = ci$dummies, excluded = ci$excluded,
>          n = nrow(data), note = note,
>          basis = "Pearson correlation of normal scores qnorm((rank - 0.5) / n), ties averaged"),
>     pd)
> }
> raw_format <- function(x) {
>   x <- as.character(x)
>   pats <- c(
>     blank_space  = "^ +$",
>     empty        = "^$",
>     integer      = "^-?[0-9]+$",
>     dec_comma    = "^-?[0-9]+,[0-9]+$",
>     dec_comma_no_leading_zero = "^-?,[0-9]+$",
>     dec_comma_scientific = "^-?[0-9]*,[0-9]+E[-+]?[0-9]+$",
>     dec_point    = "^-?[0-9]*[.][0-9]+$"
>   )
>   hit <- vapply(pats, function(p) !is.na(x) & grepl(p, x, useBytes = TRUE), logical(length(x)))
>   if (is.null(dim(hit))) hit <- matrix(hit, nrow = 1, dimnames = list(NULL, names(pats)))
>   cnt <- c(NA_value = sum(is.na(x)), colSums(hit), other = sum(!is.na(x) & rowSums(hit) == 0))
>   cnt <- cnt[cnt > 0]
>   dec <- x[!is.na(x) & grepl("^-?[0-9]*[,.][0-9]+$", x, useBytes = TRUE)]
>   ndec <- nchar(sub("^-?[0-9]*[,.]", "", dec))
>   list(
>     formats  = paste(sprintf("%s: %s", names(cnt), show_n(cnt)), collapse = "; "),
>     decimals = if (length(ndec)) sprintf("%d to %d decimals", min(ndec), max(ndec)) else ""
>   )
> }
> digit_counts <- function(x) {
>   x <- as.character(x)
>   x <- x[!is.na(x) & grepl("^-?[0-9]+$", x)]
>   if (!length(x)) return("")
>   tab <- table(nchar(sub("^-", "", x)))
>   if (length(tab) < 2) return("")
>   paste(sprintf("%s digits: %s", names(tab), show_n(as.integer(tab))), collapse = "; ")
> }
> file_info <- function(path, encoding) {
>   bytes <- readBin(path, "raw", n = min(file.size(path), 2e6))
>   crlf  <- any(bytes[-1] == as.raw(10) & bytes[-length(bytes)] == as.raw(13))
>   lines <- readLines(path, warn = FALSE, encoding = "bytes")
>   list(
>     size_bytes   = file.size(path),
>     encoding     = encoding,
>     valid_utf8   = all(validUTF8(lines)),
>     line_ending  = if (crlf) "CRLF" else "LF",
>     physical_lines = length(lines),
>     lines_with_double_quote = show_n(sum(grepl("\"", lines, useBytes = TRUE))),
>     lines_with_hash = show_n(sum(grepl("#", lines, useBytes = TRUE)))
>   )
> }
> text_summary <- function(texts, language, groups) {
>   out <- list()
>   for (g in groups) {
>     txt <- texts[[g]]
>     for (lang in c("all", sort(unique(as.character(language))))) {
>       sel <- if (lang == "all") rep(TRUE, length(txt)) else as.character(language) == lang
>       t <- txt[sel]
>       nonempty <- !is.na(t) & t != ""
>       len <- nchar(t[nonempty], type = "chars")
>       s <- num_summary(len)
>       out[[paste(g, lang)]] <- list(
>         response = g, language = lang, n = sum(sel),
>         share_of_responses = sprintf("%.3f", sum(sel) / length(txt)),
>         n_empty = show_n(sum(!nonempty)),
>         share_with_newline = fmt_share(sum(grepl("[\r\n]", t[nonempty])), sum(nonempty)),
>         share_non_ascii    = fmt_share(sum(grepl("[^ -~\r\n\t]", t[nonempty])), sum(nonempty)),
>         nchar = s
>       )
>     }
>   }
>   out
> }
> md_escape <- function(x) gsub("|", "\\|", as.character(x), fixed = TRUE)
> md_table <- function(df) {
>   df <- as.data.frame(df, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
>   df[] <- lapply(df, function(c) { c <- as.character(c); c[is.na(c)] <- ""; md_escape(c) })
>   c(paste0("| ", paste(names(df), collapse = " | "), " |"),
>     paste0("|", paste(rep("---", ncol(df)), collapse = "|"), "|"),
>     apply(df, 1, function(r) paste0("| ", paste(r, collapse = " | "), " |")),
>     "")
> }
> md_header <- function(dataset, title) {
>   c(sprintf("# Synthetic-data specification: %s", dataset), "",
>     sprintf("*%s*", title), "",
>     "> **Aggregate statistics only.** Extracted from the real (private) data by",
>     "> `synthetic/extract_spec.R` as input for a synthetic-data generator",
>     "> (Gaussian copula). It contains no row-level data, no free text and no exact",
>     "> individual values:",
>     ">",
>     "> * counts of 1-9 participants are shown as `<10`; categorical levels with",
>     ">   < 10 participants are pooled into `other` (topped up with the next-smallest",
>     ">   level until `other` has >= 10); values of ordinal variables are merged with",
>     ">   a neighbouring value; a count shown as `<10` also hides its complement (`>N`)",
>     "> * minimum and maximum (q00/q100) are exact only if >= 10 participants share",
>     ">   that value; otherwise they are bottom-/top-coded at the 10th smallest/largest",
>     ">   value (marked `*`: >= 10 participants lie at or beyond it); merged ordinal",
>     ">   cells at the ends are open-ended (`<=2`, `>=3`)",
>     "> * dummies with < 10 participants in one class are not in the correlation matrix",
>     "> * exception: sample-flow numbers (most of them reported in the manuscript)",
>     "",
>     sprintf("Created %s from embeddings `%s` (only used to rebuild the analysis samples).", Sys.Date(), EMB),
>     "")
> }
> md_flow <- function(flow) {
>   c("## 1. Sample flow", "",
>     md_table(data.frame(step = names(flow), n = unlist(lapply(flow, function(f) paste(f, collapse = "; "))))))
> }
> md_numeric <- function(num, info) {
>   out <- c("## 3. Numeric marginals (analysed sample)", "",
>            "Quantiles q00..q100 (type 7) in the analysed sample, rounded to the variable's",
>            "precision. `*` = bottom-/top-coded extreme (the 10th smallest/largest value;",
>            "the true minimum/maximum lies beyond it). `scale` = theoretical range of the",
>            "instrument or of the value labels, where known. NA share is in the sample",
>            "before the complete-case restriction (`NA base`).", "")
>   meta <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(num), function(v) {
>     s <- num[[v]]
>     data.frame(variable = v, source = info$source[[v]] %||% v, role = info$role[[v]] %||% "",
>                n = s$n, `NA base` = s$na_share, decimals = s$digits, grid = s$grid,
>                distinct = s$n_distinct,
>                scale = if (is.null(s$scale)) "" else paste(s$scale, collapse = " to "),
>                check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
>   }))
>   qt <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(num), function(v) {
>     s <- num[[v]]; q <- fmt_num(s$quantiles, s$digits)
>     if (s$q0_coded)   q[1]  <- paste0(q[1], "*")
>     if (s$q100_coded) q[21] <- paste0(q[21], "*")
>     as.data.frame(as.list(c(variable = v, setNames(q, names(s$quantiles)))), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
>   }))
>   out <- c(out, "### Variable information", "", md_table(meta), "### Quantiles", "", md_table(qt))
>   vt <- Filter(function(s) !is.null(s$values), num)
>   if (length(vt)) {
>     out <- c(out, "### Value shares of discrete variables (<= 15 distinct values)", "",
>              md_table(data.frame(variable = names(vt), values = vapply(vt, function(s)
>                paste(sprintf("%s: %s", s$values$value, s$values$share), collapse = "; "), ""))))
>   }
>   out
> }
> md_categorical <- function(cats, info) {
>   out <- c("## 4. Categorical variables (analysed sample)", "")
>   for (v in names(cats)) {
>     out <- c(out, sprintf("**%s** (source `%s`; NA base: %s; N = %d)", v,
>                           info$source[[v]] %||% v, cats[[v]]$na_share, cats[[v]]$N), "",
>              md_table(cats[[v]]$table))
>   }
>   out
> }
> md_correlation <- function(cr) {
>   R <- cr$matrix; p <- ncol(R)
>   legend <- data.frame(`#` = seq_len(p), variable = colnames(R), check.names = FALSE)
>   mat <- matrix(formatC(R, format = "f", digits = 2), nrow = p)
>   mat[upper.tri(mat)] <- ""
>   w <- 6
>   header <- paste0(formatC("", width = 4), paste(formatC(seq_len(p), width = w), collapse = ""))
>   rows <- vapply(seq_len(p), function(i)
>     paste0(formatC(i, width = 3), " ", paste(formatC(mat[i, ], width = w), collapse = "")), "")
>   dummies <- if (is.null(cr$dummies)) data.frame() else cr$dummies
>   c("## 5. Correlation matrix", "",
>     sprintf("%s. N = %d. %s.", cr$basis, cr$n, cr$note),
>     sprintf("Positive definiteness: %s; minimum eigenvalue %.4f; largest change from the rounded matrix %.2f.",
>             cr$method, cr$min_eigenvalue, cr$max_abs_change), "",
>     "Variables (dummies: `variable=level`, 1 = level, 0 = any other level):", "",
>     md_table(legend),
>     if (nrow(dummies)) c("Dummy reference levels (most frequent level):", "",
>                          md_table(unique(dummies[, c("variable", "reference")]))),
>     if (length(cr$excluded)) c("Left out of the matrix:", "", paste("*", cr$excluded), ""),
>     "Lower triangle:", "", "```", header, rows, "```", "")
> }
> md_text <- function(tx, extra = NULL) {
>   tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(tx, function(t) {
>     q <- fmt_num(t$nchar$quantiles, 0)
>     if (t$nchar$q0_coded)   q[1]  <- paste0(q[1], "*")
>     if (t$nchar$q100_coded) q[21] <- paste0(q[21], "*")
>     data.frame(response = t$response, language = t$language, n = t$n,
>                share = t$share_of_responses, empty = t$n_empty,
>                newline = t$share_with_newline, non_ascii = t$share_non_ascii,
>                q00 = q[1], q05 = q[2], q10 = q[3], q25 = q[6], q50 = q[11],
>                q75 = q[16], q90 = q[19], q95 = q[20], q100 = q[21],
>                stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
>   }))
>   c("## 6. Free-text responses", "",
>     "Length in characters of the displayed text (embedded text without the `passage: ` prefix),",
>     "non-empty responses only. `share` = share of the responses in this language;",
>     "`newline`/`non_ascii` = share of non-empty responses containing a line break / a",
>     "non-ASCII character. All 21 quantiles are in the .rds; `*` = bottom-/top-coded extreme.", "",
>     md_table(tab), extra)
> }
> `%||%` <- function(a, b) if (is.null(a)) b else a
> zv <- function(x) if (length(x)) paste(x, collapse = ", ") else "none"
> write_spec <- function(spec, md) {
>   saveRDS(spec, file.path(OUT_DIR, paste0(spec$dataset, ".rds")))
>   con <- file(file.path(OUT_DIR, paste0(spec$dataset, ".md")), "w", encoding = "UTF-8")

>   close(con)
>   message("written: ", spec$dataset)
> }
> describe_sample <- function(smp_data, vars, base_data, source, scales = list(), labels = list()) {
>   num <- list(); cats <- list()
>   for (v in vars) {
>     x <- smp_data[[v]]
>     base_x <- base_data[[source[[v]] %||% v]]
>     if (is.factor(x) || is.character(x)) {
>       ct <- cat_table(x, labels[[v]])
>       cats[[v]] <- list(table = ct$table, N = ct$N, na_share = na_share(base_x))
>     } else {
>       s <- num_summary(x, scales[[v]])
>       s$na_share <- if (any(is.na(x))) na_share(x) else na_share(base_x)
>       num[[v]] <- s
>     }
>   }
>   list(numeric = num, categorical = cats)
> }

> dummy_group_size <- function(dummy, categorical, N) {
>   var <- sub("=.*", "", dummy)
>   lev <- sub("^[^=]*=", "", dummy)
>   tab <- categorical[[var]]$table
>   if (is.null(tab)) return(NA_real_)
>   n <- as_count(tab$n[tab$level == lev])
>   if (length(n) != 1 || is.na(n)) return(NA_real_)
>   min(n, N - n)
> }
> coarsen_correlation <- function(cr, categorical) {
>   vars  <- cr$variables
>   dummy <- grepl("=", vars)
>   size  <- vapply(vars, function(v) {
>     if (!grepl("=", v)) return(Inf)
>     dummy_group_size(v, categorical, cr$n)
>   }, numeric(1))
>   keep <- !dummy | (!is.na(size) & size >= PUB_MIN_GROUP)
>   ## a principal submatrix of a positive definite matrix stays positive definite
>   m <- cr$matrix[keep, keep]
>   stopifnot(min(eigen(m, only.values = TRUE)$values) > 0)
>   list(variables = vars[keep], n = cr$n, note = cr$note, basis = cr$basis,
>        matrix = m,
>        dummies = cr$dummies[cr$dummies$dummy %in% vars[keep], , drop = FALSE],
>        left_out = c(vars[!keep], cr$excluded))
> }

SPSS data without syntax

An SPSS data file (.sav/.por) is present but no SPSS syntax file (.sps) was found, so the analysis that produced the results cannot be reproduced from the deposit. This is treated as a reproducibility failure (red). Consider depositing the analysis in jamovi (.omv) or JASP (.jasp) instead: these formats store the data and the analyses together in one file, so the results are reproducible from the file itself.

More detail

Power Analysis Check

No power analyses were detected.

Power analyses need to contain the following information to be interpretable: the type of power analysis, the statistical test, the software used, sample size, critical alpha criterion, power level, effect size, and an effect size metric. In addition, it is recommended to make sure the power analysis is reproducible (by sharing the code, or a screenshot, of the power analysis), and to provide good arguments for why the study was designed to detect an effect of this size.

For an a-priori power analysis, where the sample size is determined, reporting all information would look like:

An a priori power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that for a Cohen’s d = 0.5, an alpha level of 0.05, and a desired power level of 80% required at least 64 participants in each group.

For a sensitivity power analysis, this sentence would look like:

A sensitivity power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that with 64 participants in each group, and an alpha level of 0.05, a desired power level of 80% was reached for an effect size of d = 0.5.
